az_beaver_wall_2.blurb: A small urban sport wall in Papago Park on the Tempe side, next to the dog park and only a short stroll from the road. It holds five bolted lines: a couple of easy ones around 5.6 and 5.7, a pair of mid-5.7s, plus a 5.10 and a 5.11 for stronger climbers. The wall catches the morning sun. Because it sits in plain view of the street, expect steady road and aircraft noise, and glass and litter on the ground, so keep your rope and pack off the dirt.

az_altar_the.blurb: A dome in Stewart Pocket, southeast of Payson, that turns its face to the north. Five lines, three sport and two trad, split between a single 5.8+ and four around 5.10. The granite in this part of Arizona is described as mostly solid. Expect a hike of about twenty minutes, with the last stretch steepening onto slabs, and aim for the left side of the formation when you arrive. Quickdraws and a small trad rack cover everything here.

az_beach_the.blurb: A sport crag in Upper Devils Canyon, in the Queen Creek Canyon zone of central Arizona, east of Oak Flat. Five bolted routes run from the low 5.10s through two in the 5.11 range and a 5.12 up to a 5.13, making it a place for harder sport climbing rather than a beginner stop. Sun hits the wall early, then shade takes over in the afternoon, which is why it is considered a workable option on hot summer days.
